conventions.convention: Finite GL principal series use n≥1, prime-power q and complex representations. The Weyl group is the monomial quotient N/T≅S_n, including q=2; character coordinates transform by (w·χ)_j=χ_{w⁻¹(j)}.
The generic Hecke normalization is (T_i−v)(T_i+1)=0. H_v(0)=H_v(1)=Z[v±1]; specialization requires the parameter image to be a unit. Finite spherical generators have eigenvalues q and −1.

Right multiplication reverses composition: R_aR_b=R_ba. Standard endomorphism intertwiners consequently use B_w=R_{Θ_{w⁻¹}}, with Θ_w=q^{ℓ(w)}e_χẇe_χ and covariance compensation for alternative representatives.

For unsorted characters, stabilizer Coxeter length is intrinsic rather than ambient inversion length. The Hecke basis is transported from Weyl-sorted coordinates; in those coordinates its normalization is T_w=(∏_r a_r(−1)^{−ℓ(w_r)})B_w.

The Burau cover exists for n≥1. Positive meridians have winding 1; t is the positive deck generator and acts on the left. Unreduced relative homology uses the entire fibre over the boundary basepoint.

Burau matrices act on columns, with the rightmost word factor acting first. The relative basis is e_i=t^{i−1}ε_i and generator block is [[1−t,t],[1,0]]. The fixed reduced basis is b_i=t^i(ε_i−ε_{i+1}), carried to g_i=te_i−e_{i+1}.

The invariant covector is σ=(1,t,…,t^{n−1}). The reduced module is ker σ, whereas the invariant line is generated by (1,…,1). Their invariant direct-sum splitting is asserted over Q(t), not over the integral Laurent ring.
The Markov tower starts at n=1, with trace(1)=1, restriction compatibility, cyclicity and tr_{n+1}(xT_n)=z tr_n(x). Its negative factor is z_−=v⁻¹(z+1−v).
In the HOMFLYPT coefficient ring, v,z,u,s are units, s²=v and vzu²=z+1−v. Set α=(uz)⁻¹, l=us and m=s−s⁻¹. Division by m is licensed only after localizing at m.
P(cl β)=u^{e(β)}α^{n−1}tr_n(π_nβ) for n≥1, P(unknot)=1 and P(empty)=uz separately. Jones specialization is z=−1/(v+1), u=s, t=s²; positive σ_1³ has value t+t³−t⁴.

For nonempty oriented links, the Alexander module is absolute H_1 of the total-linking cyclic cover. Δ is gcd E_0, with ambiguity ±t^k. The library's D is Δ/(1−t) for knots and Δ for multiple components.

Morton's multivariable invariant specialized to equal labels is Δ(t)/(1−t) for any component count. The absolute one-variable determinant formula retains the factor (1−t); the knot-only normalization must not be substituted for a multi-component link.

AC is explicit for Tits deformation and its constituent-labeling consequences, geometric Burau comparisons, and oriented-link/Alexander constructions. Algebraic matrix, trace-recursion and finite lifting calculations do not independently introduce AC.

load_bearing.statement: The elements T_w, w∈S_n, form a Z[v±1]-basis of H_v(n), of rank n!, and T_wT_i is T_{ws_i} when length increases, or (v−1)T_w+vT_{ws_i} when length decreases. No choice principle is used.

Assume AC. The topological action on U in the frozen relative basis is ρ_n^mat for every braid. On the reduced basis g_i=te_i−e_{i+1}, σ_j sends g_{j−1} to g_{j−1}+g_j, g_j to −tg_j and g_{j+1} to tg_j+g_{j+1}, fixing the other basis vectors. For n=3, the full twist has image t³I_2.
There exists a unique Markov trace on the type-A tower over Z[v±1,z]. It satisfies tr_n(T_i)=z and tr_{n+1}(xT_ny)=z tr_n(xy), and is computed recursively along the previous-level free basis.

Assume AC. P is unchanged by conjugation and both Markov stabilizations. Braids with ambient-isotopic oriented closures have equal P-values; this defines an oriented-link invariant in R, normalized by P(unknot)=1 and P(empty)=uz.

Assume AC and n≥2. With strand-variable identifications forced by the braid permutation, the closed-braid-and-axis multivariable invariant is det(I−x B̄_β), up to Laurent units. Axis deletion gives det(I−B̄_β)/(1−∏t_i). The absolute one-variable polynomial is Δ_clβ(t)≍(1−t)det(I−B_β(t))/(1−t^n), for knots and links.

Assume AC for the Tits conclusion. For any torus character χ with equal-character block sizes n_r, End_G I(χ)≅⊗_r H_q(S_{n_r}), with every parameter q. In sorted coordinates its Hecke basis is λ_wB_w; for unsorted characters it is transported from the sorted module. Consequently the algebra is semisimple and abstractly isomorphic to C[W_χ], preserving simple-module dimensions. The Hecke identification itself is choice-free.

Assume AC. If X=D(f)⊂A¹_C is nonempty and A is a unital associative C[z,1/f]-algebra free of finite rank, any two semisimple fibers A_x,A_y are isomorphic as C-algebras. In particular H_q(S_n)≅e_B C[GL_n(F_q)]e_B≅C[S_n], preserving simple-module numbers and dimensions.

For a finite-dimensional semisimple complex algebra A and finite-dimensional semisimple module M=⊕_i V_i^{m_i}, End_A(M)≅∏_i M_{m_i}(C). Its simple modules are Hom_A(V_i,M), of dimensions m_i, and these index the constituents of M. The zero-module case and transport through an abstract algebra isomorphism are included; no choice principle is used.

For n≥1, H(n+1) is free on the displayed n+1 minimal-coset representatives over H(n), on the left and with inverse representatives on the right. Multiplication x⊗y↦xT_ny identifies H(n)⊗_{H(n−1)}H(n) with H(n)T_nH(n), giving H(n+1)=H(n)⊕H(n)T_nH(n) as bimodules; H(0)=Λ.

Assume AC for braid equivariance. The pair sequence is 0→M_red→U→Λ_1→Z→0, with ∂_*(e_i)=t^{i−1}(t−1), augmentation Λ_1→Z, and image M_red=ker σ. The sequence and connecting-map computation are choice-free; no integral invariant complement is asserted.
Assume AC. For Artin words x,y∈B_n and 1≤i≤n−1, the closures of xσ_i y, xσ_i⁻¹y and xy satisfy l⁻¹P(L_+)−lP(L_−)=mP(L_0), equivalently u⁻¹P_+−vuP_−=(v−1)P_0; P(unknot)=1.

alerts.finding: F10 cites thm-the-homflypt-skein-relation as: “Its skein relation is l^{-1}P(L_+)-lP(L_-)=mP(L_0).” Proof 6.1 then uses this for skein uniqueness on oriented diagrams. The cited supplier's Statement explicitly restricts its triple to closures of xσ_i y, xσ_i^{-1}y and xy in one B_n. The consumer does not carry that restriction or explicitly extend the supplier's P-identity to general triples. Its own Proof 3.1 gives a common-picture braiding argument for the Euler invariant, and Birman–Brendle equation (18) supplies a general source statement, but neither is explicitly applied to P in F10/6.1. The coefficient homomorphism and normalization calculation themselves agree with the owned suppliers.

seams_checked.note: The categorification theorem correctly retains AC, the coefficient-ring unit requirements, s²=v, vzu²=z+1−v, α=(uz)⁻¹ and the normalization P(unknot)=1. Its substitution gives l↦t⁻¹, m↦q⁻¹−q and α↦(t⁻¹−t)/(q−q⁻¹). The skein citation suppresses the supplier's braided-triple hypothesis, as detailed in the alert.

Opened the decategorification proposition, bigrading/local-index definition and five-strand kernel lemma. The Burau block is preserved after the explicit zero-based relabeling, with columns and ordinary product order retained; the displayed conjugation uses q=t. The kernel lemma retains AC and the integral reduced/unreduced same-kernel bridge, and explicitly uses clockwise s_i=σ_i⁻¹. Its displayed free-word certificate was executed successfully. The iterated Laurent-ring use preserves finite coefficient uniqueness and monomial units.
